checks.explanation: Donald Trump won the 2024 presidential election and was sworn in for a second term in January 2025, confirming this prediction.

Oil prices did not spike dramatically after the 2024 election regardless of who won; global oil prices remained relatively range-bound to lower through 2025-2026 amid ample supply, and Trump himself pursued a 'drill baby drill' expansion agenda rather than facing Democratic restrictions.

Trump signed an executive order in March 2025 directing the dismantling of the Department of Education and shifting authority back toward the states, matching the prediction (though full legal elimination still requires Congress).

US electricity demand growth projections tied to AI data centers through the mid-2020s to 2030s called for roughly doubling to tripling generation capacity, consistent with the prediction and driving major buildout plans across gas, nuclear, and renewables.
The Trump administration did not deploy US ground troops to fight in Ukraine; US involvement remained limited to diplomatic, financial, and intelligence support rather than direct combat deployment.

Iran had not obtained a nuclear weapon by late September 2024 or in the following two years; instead, Israeli and US strikes targeted Iran's nuclear facilities in June 2025 amid ongoing concerns about but no confirmed acquisition of a weapon.
Trump did not support or sign a federal abortion ban during his second term; abortion policy remained governed at the state level.

No automatic green-card-with-diploma policy for college graduates was implemented; instead the Trump administration pursued restrictive immigration policies, including tighter rules on foreign student and skilled-worker visas.
The Trump administration released tens of thousands of pages of previously classified JFK assassination files in March 2025, early in the new term, matching the prediction.
Biden did not win a second term to implement his tax agenda, so this conditional prediction about a fourfold tax increase was never put to the test.

Trump did implement a broad, aggressive tariff plan once reelected, including the April 2025 'Liberation Day' tariffs covering nearly all trading partners, contradicting the prediction that he would not follow through.

Trump's tariff plan was not meaningfully scaled back or narrowed; it was implemented broadly across nearly all trading partners and goods categories starting April 2025, contrary to the prediction of a toned-down rollout.
